resolution: The sources read here take being analogically: Aristotle's pros hen (STMT-BEING-SAID-PROS-HEN), Aquinas' analogy of divine names (STMT-DIVINE-NAMES-ANALOGICAL), being as the first analogical predicate (STMT-BEING-FIRST-ANALOGICAL-PREDICATE), and grades of being by approach to God (STMT-BEING-MEASURED-BY-APPROACH-TO-GOD). The quarta via premises that speak of more and less in being (STMT-GRADES-HAVE-A-MAXIMUM, STMT-MOST-TRUE-IS-MOST-BEING, STMT-MAXIMUM-IN-GENUS-CAUSES-ALL-IN-GENUS) are to be read in this analogical sense. Their Lean form does not encode it: `MoreIn esse` is a primitive comparative compatible with both senses. The two senses now have order models (DEF-HOMOGENEOUS-SCALE for the univocal sense, DEF-ORDER-BY-APPROACH-TO-A-PRIMARY for attribution), and DISAMB-ORDER-OF-BEING records, premise by premise, which survive on which model. The one passage between senses it finds is STMT-CAUSE-OF-QUALITY-IN-ANOTHER-IS-MORE-SUCH: its source sense is synonymous (univocal), and its use at being with the primary as effect (AQUINAS-ST-I-Q2-A3-FIRST-MOVER-IS-FIRST-BEING) has no support in the analogical sense; its use with the primary as cause does (STMT-ATTRIBUTION-ORDER-RESTRICTS-CAUSE-MORE-SUCH).
